_: The breast: its skin over the breast's soft tissue (fat and fibroglandular tissue together), the pectoralis and the ribs, as a compliance stack for contact (a garment's pressure, a hand). Living, quasi-static, small strain is the case: the default breast-tissue modulus is the living suction measurement (DURAES24, 196 women) that ex vivo indentation agrees with (SAMANI07); whole-breast gravity fits read softer, dynamic elastography stiffer (BREAST_TISSUE section 0), so it is TUNABLE per person. Optics, thermal, states start as skin.body's (E). fs-cloth lane, 11-11.

loss_factor_impact.src: the slap is carried by the fat and muscle under the skin: fat from fat.subcutaneous (GRIG17 Prony, computed; E for trunk fat), wobble from SOFTTISSUE M31 (2 zeta). The skin's own tan delta at 10 Hz is 0.06-0.16 (BOYER07). how a solver uses it: integrate the Prony set (deform.viscoelastic.prony) as internal variables in an implicit step (one exponential update per term per step; stable at any dt) on top of the hyperelastic stress, so a 1-10 ms slap sees the short-time stiffness and loses energy in the 1-10 ms terms; do not use Rayleigh damping fitted to the ~15 Hz wobble: beta-damping gives zeta = beta * omega / 2, so a beta set for zeta 0.15 at 15 Hz (beta 3.2 ms) gives zeta ~5 at 250-500 Hz (a 1-2 ms pulse): over-damped, the slap goes dead. Where only one number fits, use the loss factor at the pulse's frequency f ~ 1 / (2 x contact time), zeta = tan_delta / 2.
